scenario_text: A point mass is constrained to move at constant speed along a circular track in an inertial frame. Across independent trials, its mass, tangential speed, and track radius are varied, and the inward constraint-force magnitude is recorded after steady circular motion is established. Friction and changes in speed are excluded, so the response arises only from the continuous redirection of velocity. The benchmark seeks the instantaneous radial force magnitude from the sampled conditions.

spec.target_description: Magnitude of the inward radial force required to maintain steady circular motion, in newtons.

input_symbols.description: Tangential speed, in meters per second.
Radius of the circular track, in meters.

expected_behaviors: The force is nonnegative throughout the sampled domain.
At fixed speed and radius, the response grows linearly with mass.
At fixed mass and radius, the response grows quadratically with speed.
At fixed mass and speed, the response decreases inversely with radius.
The response tends toward zero as the speed tends toward zero.
forbidden_behaviors: Dependence on elapsed time, orbital phase, or initial position.
Tangential drag, propulsion, or speed-changing force terms.
Sign changes within the positive input domain.

scenario_text: A point-like bob on a massless, fixed-length arm swings in a vertical plane about a frictionless pivot. The arm length and uniform gravitational background are held fixed, while angular displacement and angular velocity evolve together from each initial condition. The target is the instantaneous rate of change of angular velocity produced by the angle-dependent restoring torque. Trials remain in the oscillatory regime, with no external forcing, damping, or motion of the support.

spec.target_description: Instantaneous angular acceleration of the swinging bob, in radians per second squared.

required_dynamic_states.description: Angular displacement from the downward equilibrium orientation, in radians.
Angular velocity, in radians per second.

expected_behaviors: Angular displacement and angular velocity evolve jointly along each trajectory.
The angular acceleration vanishes at the downward equilibrium orientation.
The restoring acceleration reverses sign when the angular displacement reverses.
The angle dependence is periodic and bounded rather than polynomially unbounded.
Within the selected regime, trajectories repeatedly exchange angular speed and displacement without decay.
forbidden_behaviors: Damping, driven forcing, or time-dependent coefficients.
A restoring acceleration that is globally linear in angular displacement.
Dependence on independently sampled dynamic states outside the trajectory.
